title: Integral radicial surjections preserve the category of etale algebraic spaces
statement: Let $B$ be a scheme and work with algebraic spaces over $B$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], using sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be representable, integral, universally injective and surjective. Explicitly, for every scheme $T$ and morphism $T\to Y$, the fibre product $X_T=X\times_YT$ is a scheme and $X_T\to T$ is integral [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], surjective on scheme points, and universally injective (every further scheme base change is injective on point sets). For an algebraic space $H$, let $\operatorname{EtSp}(H)$ have objects all algebraic spaces $V$ equipped with a chartwise etale map $V\to H$ [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence], meaning that its composite with every representable etale scheme chart of $V$ is representable etale, and arrows all morphisms of algebraic spaces over $H$. Then the base-change functor $$\operatorname{EtSp}(Y)\longrightarrow\operatorname{EtSp}(X),\qquad (V\to Y)\longmapsto (X\times_YV\to X)$$ is an equivalence of categories. No quasi-compactness, separation, finite-presentation or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 05ZH (theorem-topological-invariance), full statement; etale algebraic-space objects use the chartwise notion, not a representability assumption on their structure maps.

proof.text: Base change is well defined by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. Choose a representable surjective etale scheme atlas $W\to Y$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Put $A=X\times_YW$, $R=W\times_YW$ and $T=W\times_YW\times_YW$. The atlas and fibre-product statements show that $A,R,T$ are schemes and $A\to X$ is a surjective etale atlas. By the explicit scheme-test hypothesis on $f$, the maps $f_W:A\to W$, $f_R:X\times_YR\to R$ and $f_T:X\times_YT\to T$ are integral, universally injective and surjective. By [lem-pc-integral-radicial-surjective-universal-homeomorphism] each is a scheme universal homeomorphism, and [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance] makes its inverse image an equivalence on sheaves of sets. Fix one common universe bound for the sites, charts and sheaves used here, allowing the generator coproducts in [lem-sfb-space-etale-sheaf-realization]. No geometric finiteness assumption enters this choice.

source.place: Atlas reduction of Tag 05ZH; scheme invariance: etale-cohomology.tex Tag 04DZ. Size convention: spaces-properties.tex Tag 0GF6. Characterization: morphisms.tex Tag 04DF (lemma-universal-homeomorphism).

proof.text: First prove that $f^{-1}:\operatorname{Sh}(Y_{\mathrm{et}})\to\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{et}})$ is fully faithful. Its restriction to $A$ is $f_W^{-1}$ of restriction to $W$: both are the inverse image along the same composite $A\to Y$, by [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. The same observation holds on $X\times_YR$ and $X\times_YT$. Given $c:f^{-1}F\to f^{-1}G$, restrict it to $A$. Full faithfulness of $f_W^{-1}$ gives a unique $b:F|_W\to G|_W$ with that pullback. The two sides of the descent compatibility equation for $b$ on $R$ become equal under $f_R^{-1}$, since $c$ is global on $X$; faithfulness of $f_R^{-1}$ makes them equal. Atlas descent [lem-sfb-space-atlas-sheaf-descent] glues $b$ to a unique $a:F\to G$. On $A$ the maps $f^{-1}a$ and $c$ agree, so they agree globally by the faithful restriction part of atlas descent for $A\to X$. Finally, if two maps $a$ have the same pullback, faithfulness on $W$ makes their restrictions equal and faithful atlas restriction makes the maps equal. This proves both fullness and faithfulness.

source.place: Tag 05ZH, full faithfulness, implemented by spaces-properties.tex Tag 05YY and scheme invariance rather than the defective closed-graph assertion.

proof.text: For essential surjectivity, let $K$ be a sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$. Scheme invariance for $f_W$ gives a sheaf $G$ on $W_{\mathrm{et}}$ and an isomorphism $\theta:f_W^{-1}G\simeq K|_A$. The canonical descent isomorphism for $K|_A$ on $A\times_XA=X\times_YR$, conjugated by the two pullbacks of $\theta$, is an isomorphism between the pullbacks of $p_1^{-1}G$ and $p_2^{-1}G$. By fullness of $f_R^{-1}$ it lifts to a map $\alpha:p_1^{-1}G\to p_2^{-1}G$; lift its inverse too. Faithfulness makes the two composites identities, so $\alpha$ is invertible. On $T$ the cocycle equation for $\alpha$ becomes the cocycle equation for the canonical datum of $K$ after $f_T^{-1}$. Its faithfulness therefore proves the equation on $T$. Atlas descent gives $F$ on $Y$ with descent pair $(G,\alpha)$. The isomorphism $\theta$ is compatible with descent by the definition of $\alpha$, so atlas descent for $A\to X$ glues it to $f^{-1}F\simeq K$. The restriction identifications used here are the composition comparisons of the canonical small-etale morphism. Together with the previous step this proves that $f^{-1}$ is an equivalence.

source.place: Scheme input: etale-cohomology.tex Tag 04DZ; atlas descent and cocycle: spaces-properties.tex Tag 05YY; composition: Tag 03G2.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-etale-sheaf-realization] over $Y$ and $X$. Its explicit construction identifies the functor on spaces with the sheaf equivalence just proved: for every sheaf $F$ on $Y$ and scheme test $T\xrightarrow{x}X$, both $X\times_YE_Y(F)$ and $E_X(f^{-1}F)$ have sections $(x,s)$ with $s\in\Gamma(T,(fx)^{-1}F)=\Gamma(T,x^{-1}f^{-1}F)$. The equality is the canonical composition comparison of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model], and commutes with restriction and sheaf maps. Hence it gives a natural isomorphism of algebraic spaces over $X$. The natural counits $E_H(h_V)\simeq V$ identify this with the given base-change functor on every object and arrow. Conjugating $f^{-1}$ by the two realization equivalences therefore proves exactly that $V\mapsto X\times_YV$ is an equivalence on all chartwise etale algebraic spaces. This includes objects with nonrepresentable or nonseparated structure maps.

Sources read: Stacks 05ZH (statement and whole proof), 05YY (lemma-descent-sheaf) and 0GF6 (the construction, statement and size footnote). The item statement matches 05ZH (f representable, integral, universally injective, surjective; EtSp means all chartwise-étale spaces) and is neither weakened nor changed; the parent thickening node still gets what it cites. The source error is real: the graph of c is a section of an étale map, so it is open, but it is closed only when V is separated over Y. The doubled-origin-line counterexample is correct, and the delivery's route avoids that step. Step 1: W, R, T are schemes by the fibre-product node; A, X×R, X×T are schemes by the item's scheme-test hypothesis; then 04DF gives universal homeomorphisms (lem-pc) and thm-weil-pbc gives that u^{-1} is an equivalence. Step 2: full faithfulness of f^{-1}, with restriction to A = f_W^{-1}∘restriction by the composition clause of the site model, a lift on W, the compatibility on R by faithfulness, and gluing and equality on the atlases W→Y and A→X by the arrow part of the descent node. Step 3: essential surjectivity by descending (G, α), with the cocycle on T by faithfulness and θ glued. Step 4: the explicit (x,s) calculation gives X×_Y E_Y ≅ E_X∘f^{-1}, and with the counits this is the actual base-change functor; no representability or separation of V is used. New nodes: atlas-descent (05YY) and realization (0GF6 over an algebraic-space base, size hypothesis explicit) are both true, satisfy B1-B7 with all three search kinds recorded, and are not clauses of the item. They are not duplicates of lem-a1-etale-sheaf-algebraic-space-realization (scheme base only), lem-pe-site-sheaf-gluing (04TR, existence only), the fppf-level 0ADT nodes def-sfb-space-cover-sheaf-descent-categories and lem-sfb-fppf-space-datum-sheaf-realization, lem-sfb-etale-sheaf-space-atlas-bootstrap (0BH4) or the Rydh node (needs quasi-separated spaces). The item is still unsplit in live, and neither new id exists there. lem-pc and thm-weil-pbc lie inside the unit's route; the four declared tool uses are accepted as generic foundations.
